units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: I have read this thread from the gallery over three nights. A lighthouse is a building whose whole purpose is to let other people see the ground, or rather the rocks. We never see it ourselves; the beam is too bright and it goes outward, away from us. I find that a comfort. The light is not for the keeper.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Kennel night attendant, late to this. My ground is the yard between the kennel blocks, lit by one lamp on a pole, and the dogs know the edge of it better than I do. On the last walk they'll go right up to where the light stops and sit. Every one of them, the same spot. I paced it once: eleven steps from the pole.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Wind's up here tonight, so no lifts. I'm sat in the cab waiting for it to drop, with rain running down the glass. I'll be honest, I've enjoyed this thread more than anything in months, and I've read every single reply.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: The rain's come in over the island. The fire in the yard is lower tonight; nobody went out to bank it. From the desk you can see the shine of the wet trunks at the edge of the light, and then nothing. The ground between the yard and the first trees is the part you can't see.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Wren, I'm asking you directly to stop. Whatever this is, it is frightening people who work alone at night, including some who have messaged me privately. If you're struggling, tell someone in daylight. If you're playing, it isn't a game anyone else agreed to.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: I'm not going to read any more of these, I'm sorry. I've got eleven people asleep in this building and I need to be the calm one tonight. Wren, I hope you're all right, whoever and wherever you are.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Retail park, top deck of the multi-storey. I can see the ground fine, it's six floors down and covered in trolleys. What I can't see is the bit past the lights where the bypass embankment is. I walked it in daylight once. Brambles and a trolley that's been there since spring. Knowing that helps more than you'd think.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: late to the sleep tips but: ear defenders from work, the proper yellow ones, beat any foam earplug ever made. you look ridiculous. you sleep like a stone. my girlfriend calls me the bin man in the daytime, which I've decided is affectionate

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: I'm going to ask the mod to close this. I started it to pass the time and it's turned into something I don't like, and that's on me for not stopping it sooner. Sorry, everyone. Thank you to all of you who posted your cab and your corridor and your desk. Bo.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Porter sleep tips: don't nap in the hospital car park before you drive home. You wake up stiff, confused and parked at a strange angle. Ask me how I know. Also, the blackout curtains from the Saturday market are a third of the price of the posh ones and just as dark.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Asking the mod to close this one before it turns into a mattress review site. I started it for cab views and it's ended with earplugs, which is honestly the most night-shift thing that could have happened. Sorry to anyone I kept awake, and thanks, all of you. Bo.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Whatever this thread has turned into, I'd like to say the plain thing. If you're on a night shift somewhere remote tonight, I hope your heater works, your relief turns up on time, and somebody somewhere is thinking of you kindly. Tollinby, two in the morning, kettle on, rain on the shop window.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: If you're reading this on an island with trees outside the window, don't look out.

units.author: lh_wren_nights
units.text: Sorry. That was a stupid thing to post. I'm on my third night and I'm frightening myself. I'm going to log off and drink a glass of water, like the mod always says. Goodnight, all of you.

units.title: Housekeeping
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: that thread is now closed. That's all I'm going to say about it tonight. Drink some water, everyone, and look after the person on the next shift.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Thanks, mod. Off to do the four o'clock run. Kettle's on in the porters' lodge if anyone's passing Port Ammet General, and the biscuits are the good ones tonight.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Back. Sorry about that. The camera's infrared had flicked on and I wanted to watch it rather than type. It was a fox. Camera 3, row K, sitting by the fence, limp in the back left leg. It got up and went under the fence at 02:41. Logged as fox. Tonight: patrolled, nil found.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: a fox!! called it. a fox with a limp is a fox with a backstory. what are we calling it, because the warehouse has already voted and it's 'Gary'

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Thank you for coming back to say what it was. That's how it should be done, and it's rarer on forums than it ought to be. Most stories here just stop.

units.title: The man at the edge of the forecourt
units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Update on the man who stands at the edge of the forecourt light, the one I went out to and who turned out to be waiting for a lift. He's back. Different coat now, long and dark instead of the anorak. Same spot, same way of standing. I'm not sure it's the same man. I didn't go out this time. I sold a lot of pies.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: Same city, other side of the river. Do you want me to come by after the lab? I can buy a pie and stand next to you looking stern. I'm extremely good at looking stern after nineteen hours awake.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Kind of you. He's gone now. A car pulled up at the far side and he wasn't there when it left. Probably got in. Probably. Come by anyway, the pies are half price after four.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Coat changes are the worst for identifying people. Control once had me log the same bloke as three different suspects because he kept taking his hoodie on and off. Mind you, he was nicking trolleys. Yours is probably just cold.

units.title: A&E: the outage regulars
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Busy one. Since the cuts started, the A&E board is full of the same story: fell over in the dark. Tonight we had two ankles, a man who walked into his own wheelie bin, and a lady who missed her bottom stair because she was carrying a candle and a cat at the same time. Everybody fine, nobody happy. Buy a head torch, Port Ammet.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Same here when our grid went last winter. The candle-and-cat combination is a classic. We started calling cold snaps 'ankle season'. Back to it.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Falls rise sharply during blackouts, especially among older people on stairs and thresholds. If anyone's reading with an elderly relative nearby: a plug-in nightlight with a battery that switches on when the mains fails costs very little and is worth more than any advice I could give.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I sold a great many candles this week, which I don't normally stock, and I shall now feel personally responsible for the cat. Get well, all of you, and carry one thing at a time.

units.title: Rain's here (wherever 'here' is)
units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text:
rain tonight in Halvard, every fare wants dropping at the door not the corner, fair enough
anyway had a lady with a cello in the back who told me the whole plot of an opera between the station and the river, it ends badly, everyone dies of being sad

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Rain in Coriveth too, the first in weeks. The white van's gone from the market steps, by the way. The traders say they never saw anyone get in or out. I've thrown away the greaseproof with the plate on it. Brioche tonight, very buttery, very consoling.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Weyhaven's not raining exactly, it's just damp, like a towel. aisle 41 has a leak in the roof so we've got a bucket, a cone and a sign that says caution in three languages. the bucket has become a sort of mascot

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Rain in Port Ammet and the studio roof is singing. Tonight's phone-in was all about lamps in windows. Everyone's got one now. One caller has six, one in every room that faces the sea. I'm still not buying any of it, but they were the nicest calls I've had all year.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Rain up top, dry below. Two kilometres in, you'd never know. Bus home is going to be grim. Streetlights back on in town tonight, for what it's worth. Nobody in the doorways.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Wishing you both a dry night, though I gather from the wireless you will not get one. Rain on a reservoir has a lovely sound on tape, rather like frying. Do write the start times on the boxes. Regards, Ned

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Setting up. Rain since lunchtime, steady but soft, not much wind yet. Blimps on, windshields on. Position one is on the north shore below the dam path as planned. Tern is at the old pumping house. Voice channel open. Clap test at 23:28 on all recorders. Make of it what you will.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good luck. Remember that drips on a blimp are very sharp transients with almost no low end; anything in the woods should carry some low-frequency energy. Note which is which as you go if you can, and keep away from the sluice boards.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I'm in position, the pumping house door keeps banging in the gusts so I've wedged it with a stone. clap heard on the channel, synced, clocks agree to under a second. it is extremely wet. the binaural head is wearing a carrier bag and looks miserable

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: 00:15. Rain steady. Owls quiet, which you'd expect in this. Two percussive events at 23:58 and 00:07 on the dish, toward the north ride, both soft; could be drips off the pines onto the dish hood. Logged both. Water's up at the shore, a metre further in than last week.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: 00:45. Half an hour of nothing but rain. Tern had one event at the pumping house at 00:29 that I didn't get. The dam is too exposed in this, so I'm going to move to position two on the outflow path by the sluice with the handheld and leave position one running.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: 01:14. Moving to position two now. Back on the channel in about ten minutes.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: dunlin? it's been half an hour. your channel went to nothing about a quarter past one, not static, just nothing. probably the app. I've got a knock here at 01:31 and another at 01:33 and I'd really love to know if you got them at two

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so still nothing. I've tried ringing, straight to voicemail. it's chucking it down now. I'm staying put, because if I go wandering about in this I'll end up in the reservoir myself. dunlin if you're reading this just post a full stop or something

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Tern, stay where you are and stay safe. Phones die in cold and wet far faster than people expect, and voice apps drop out the moment the signal does. If you haven't heard from him by first light, ring the estate office. Please don't go down to the sluice in the dark on your own.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: packing up. my files ran till 03:30 like we said. no full stop from him. I'm not going down to two in this, the path's under water past the boards, I can hear it from here. the lane's starting to flood, so I'm going home before I can't. I'll come back in daylight if he hasn't posted.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: home. soaked. his profile says last active 01:14. he's an adult with a car and a brother in Tollinby and he is probably asleep. I'm just going to say that to myself a few times and try to sleep as well.

units.title: Rain on the harbour: hydrophone test
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Rain on the harbour surface through the hydrophone tonight, for anyone who's never heard it: like bacon in a pan, all top end. The 50 Hz has gone completely under it, so no checking the ice plant pump tonight. Clip is 4 minutes, raw, no processing, gain as before.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on, and this is genuinely gorgeous. It's like standing under a tin roof in the middle of a field. Saving this one for a bad day at work.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Rain noise on water peaks well above 10 kHz; you'll see it as a bright band across the top of the spectrogram. It makes a useful calibration reference, actually. Note the rainfall rate if you can get it from wx's station.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Ice then rain this morning. Tollinby rd like glass at 06:00, gritter through at 06:20. Brackwater jct lights actually working for once, green and everything, which after the night we've had feels like an omen.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Collection achieved. A lorry arrived on Rope Walk at 06:40, the crew having opened the depot gate by hand at half past five, I'm told. Thirty-one bins emptied in nineteen minutes, which I timed. I have written to the council to thank the crew, and only the crew. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: I said hysteria and I stand by it. The rain's here now, so it'll be 'corrosion' again and you'll all have something new to blame. Mark my words, it'll be the bins next. It's always the bins.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: A note on last night. Four circuits faulted in one night, including the inland Brackwater feeder, which is nowhere near salt. If it were coastal corrosion I'd expect the coast first and the coast alone. I said I couldn't explain the clear-night trips; I'll add that I can't explain the inland one either. That's two things I can't explain, which is two more than I like.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Last night's cut here was 00:30 to 02:10. The children have stopped being scared and started being organised: the eldest has a torch rota. The baby slept through. The spaniel did not. Has anyone actually had money back from the co-op for a freezer yet?

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Not yet. I sent the form a week ago and they emailed to say it's 'in the queue'. Pebble is fine, by the way, though she has taken to sleeping on the landing facing the stairs, which is new, and which I've decided not to think about.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: For the record: last night Gilliver and Lisle went at 22:48 and every time we closed the breaker it tripped again within minutes, four times, until it finally held at 03:16. Port Ammet north went at 23:21, Brackwater at 00:27. With wx's readings that's four trip nights out of six with no fog at all. I've given the table to the office. They said thank you.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Pattern change. Pressure has fallen 14 hPa since this morning, wind backed southerly, first rain at the station at 11:40 and 9.2 mm since. The calm spell is over. For the cuts record: the next few nights will have real salt and real damp, so if the trips carry on, nobody will be able to separate the weather from whatever else it is.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: wx, that is the most ominous weather report I have ever read, and I've read a lot of them this fortnight. Lamp monitor reports bike lamp operational. Rain is very loud on the conservatory roof. Goodnight, everyone.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Rain in Tollinby now, and our power has held tonight, at least as I write. The square's one lamp is reflected in every puddle, so there are suddenly forty of them. I find I'm listening for the fridges to stop anyway, out of habit.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: May I add, since the custom is being discussed so kindly: for our class project in 1991, three children brought in their grandmothers' lamps, and not one grandmother would say what it was for. One said 'you'll know when you're older'. I am now considerably older, and I don't.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: May I ask something I have been wondering. Does anyone know whether the young people on the island have a lamp? I can see their lights from my front room most evenings, but I can't tell if any of it is a lamp in a window or only their work lights. I should like to think they have one. It is only manners, after all.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: They've a fire in the yard most nights, Mrs. That's a lamp of sorts. And there's a window lit late, you can see it from the creel line, one square of light low down by the trees. I'd call that a lamp in a window, near enough.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: They've got a generator and floodlights, love, they don't need anybody's lamp. But fair play, it's a nice thought. Don't tell anyone I said that.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I hope they do too. I'm sorry, I don't know either. I watch the same lights from my kitchen. There's one square one that stays on late, the one Bram means. I like to think it's a window with someone sitting at it.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Look at the pattern. Cuts all over the mainland every night this week. Lights on the Holm every night this week. Who has power when nobody else does? People who planned for it. That's what a refuge is: somewhere with nothing around it and its own lights. Just asking.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect if the island were being prepared as a refuge? Fuel tanks, building materials, a harbour wall, a jetty. Instead the only boat traffic in the harbour log is a weekly supply run and a barge earlier in the month. It's a clearance. An unusual one, perhaps, but a clearance.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 5: I've been contacted privately about the owner's other properties. Someone has passed me a list and I'm checking it before I post anything. Some of it already looks off. I'd rather be slow than wrong again, so please don't ask me for it yet.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: The camp has its own lights because it has its own generator, because it is on an island with no grid connection, because it is a camp. The mainland has cuts because its grid is faulting. Those two facts are connected by nothing except your sentence.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A reminder that we are now well into speculation. 'Refuge' is a theory. 'Land speculation' is also a theory, though a better documented one. Please label which you are offering. And thank you all for keeping this civil in a difficult week.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Funny how the 'boring' explanation always comes from people who read planning applications for fun. Who benefits from it being boring? Ask yourselves that.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Everyone who'd like an accurate picture of the world, mostly. I'll keep reading them, thank you, and I'll keep linking them for anyone who wants to check my working.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran

edit.text: Last thing from me on this. Corran had nothing round it either. I won't go into it.

units.text: Last thing from me on this. Corran had nothing round it either. That was the point of it, the client said, somewhere you could see a long way in every direction. I won't go into it.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I'm sorry. I hope you're all right. Thank you for saying what you did say. It helps a little, to know that someone came back from one of these and is still posting.

units.title: Holm work. Update.
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Bumping my old thread with an update. Took the hedge-cutting job in tollinby in the end, two weeks, cash, home for tea. Glad I didn't go out to the Holm, the way people are talking. No offence to the lads out there, hope they're paid proper and home soon. Tickets still valid, chainsaw and brushcutter, no job too small.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Glad you didn't? It's tree cutting, mate. The only things out there are trees and people who believe the Sound Board.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: You did right. Not for any reason I'll go into. Just that a hedge in Tollinby is a job you can walk home from every night.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Morning boat from Lisle, with the night floods still on the deck. Odd to see them in daylight: four big grey boxes on brackets, nothing special. Rain due by lunch. If the 22:40 is late tonight I'm blaming the weather and not the welfare review, which I think counts as personal growth.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Mr Brisk, if I may. I taught the first mate on that ferry and the pier attendant on Lisle, and some of their parents before them. They are not people who make things up, and they were never the sort of children who did. One may disagree about what they saw. One should not suggest they are foolish.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Nobody said foolish. I said they saw a kid. People can be honest and still wrong, Mrs Hale. That's not an insult, it's most of history.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Second night on the slip coming up... rain this time. Last night was fine, honestly fine, I only looked at the end of the slip about forty times. Ha. Thank you, Mrs Hale, for what you said, by the way. You still correct my spelling in my head.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I don't want to argue with anyone... but since people keep asking what I saw on Lisle: it wasn't tall. About my height, maybe five four, five five. Standing right where the slip goes under the water. I had my glasses in my pocket and it was drizzling, so. Maybe it was a kid, ha. I don't know.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Ada, I'm not calling you wrong about Lisle. I'm telling you what we saw at Gilliver, and it wasn't five four. It was taller than the lower bracket on the slip lamp post, which is two metres off the concrete. Dark coat to the ground. No light. I said it the first night and I'm saying it now. I stand by it.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: I'd ask everyone to remember that two people, on two different nights, in two different weathers, may well have seen two different things, and neither of them is lying. Byelaw 14 applies in every case. Thank you both for your patience with all of us.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Two metres is a big lad. The chippy lad's never been two metres in his life. Ada's five four could be him, mind, if he'd gone to Lisle, which he didn't. He's sick on the slip, never mind the crossing.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: right. two sightings, two heights, two nights. that's for the sound board not us. locking this one lads, take it there if you must and leave kerris and ada be

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engine room report, first night back: the genset took the deck load at Lisle in the cut without a flicker, the aft flood had a loose connector which I fixed with tape and language, and nobody blinded Bram's lads at the wall. Tonight's rain will be the proper test of the seals.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: First night back. Ran to time both ways. Gilliver slip clear on arrival, harbourmaster on the head, nobody on the end. Lisle the same. Shore power went at Lisle as we came alongside, and the tower's generator picked it up in about four seconds. Crew steady. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Slip was clear both ends. I looked every time we came in. Faces on the pier at Lisle, all of them people I know by name. That's what I wanted.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, skipper. The slip head will be coned again tonight from 22:00. With the rain, please take care on the lower slip, which is weeded and slippery whatever the lighting.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Patrol notes: the Gilliver spur tripped four times last night between 22:48 and 03:16. Every time we closed it, it went again within minutes, like it had been waiting. Walked the layby spans twice with a second lamp and a second person, like Garvey would want. Nothing on the line. I'm tired.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: tess you're doing the job of three. chandlery freezers lost four hours last night so we've gone on the shore genny full time. garvey if you're reading this, we miss your swearing

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Was out at the creels this morning and the layby pole had a gull on it, nothing else. Rain's here now, lass. That'll give the office its salt fog to point at, so expect a statement.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: For the record, last night at the station: 1030 hPa and falling, calm until 04:00, humidity 70 per cent and rising, no fog. Tonight is wet and windy, so from here my readings won't help anyone untangle it. I'll keep posting them anyway.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Irena love your tea is lovely and your husband was right, we are two silly women, and I don't care, I'll be there again tomorrow at five with biscuits, the good ones from the depot machine, the ones with the chocolate on both sides

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Shop notice: lift out from 10 till 1 today. I'll hold any heavy shopping behind the counter and bring it up after. Free tea at the shop door this morning for anyone waiting for daylight or a neighbour. H

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, the lift is out today, as the notice said, and Mr Benedikt kindly carried my shopping up last night. Lorna and I sat with tea this morning until it was light. I heard nothing at all on the stairs at eight o'clock, which I record also, so that it is fair. Irena, 7C

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Notice about knocking for a neighbour is now up by the lift and on the stair door of every floor. The survey request has 47 names. Kerrow say they're 'considering' it, which I'll take as a maybe. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: I have stopped counting. Not because the counts changed. Because I noticed I was counting my own steps on the way to the shop, to the bus, and up the ladder at the signal box, and I would like to stop doing that. The table is withdrawn. Thank you to those who read it.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Tobin, for what it's worth, your counts were the most careful data anyone in this building produced. I still think there's an acoustic explanation, and I'd rather find it than have you count steps forever. Look after yourself.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: tobin stopping counting is somehow the scariest post in this whole thread lol. sincerely, good for you man. i've started taking the lift too. not because of anything. because of everything, i guess

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Not sketching the landing tonight. I've drawn it twenty-six times and noticed that every version has the light a little dimmer than it really is (which says more about me than the bulb). Drawing the view from my window instead: rain on the car park, the bus shelter, the chip shop sign with one letter out.

units.title: Found: child's mitten, Mill Lane
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Found on the wall by the Mill Lane postbox this evening: one child's mitten, red with a white snowflake, soaked through. I've put it on the railings in a freezer bag so it stays dry. I know what it's like to lose something you love, even if it's only a mitten.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Not ours, all present and accounted for, but bless you for the freezer bag. Losing mittens is the third most common event in our house, after power cuts and arguments about power cuts.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Keeper was right. Reservoir lane under water at the culvert by 17:30, council closed it at 17:45, diversion via the Tollinby rd. The temp lights are now controlling a junction onto a closed road. Peak council.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Lane will be under until the rain eases. Don't drive through it, the culvert edge drops a metre. I've had one car stuck already tonight and it won't be the last. Anyone going up to the reservoir, use the top gate.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: School bus took the diversion and the kids got home forty minutes late, terribly proud of themselves for 'surviving the flood'. Thank you both for the updates; I'd have tried the lane otherwise.
